configuration.title: Poly
config.serverPath.description: Path to the poly binary. Relative paths resolve against the first workspace folder; empty uses the bundled binary, then `poly` from PATH.
config.lintOnSave.description: Publish lint diagnostics when a supported file is opened or saved.
config.format.enabled.description: Let poly rewrite files: Format Document, format-on-save, Format Selection, and the trailing-whitespace and final-newline fixes .editorconfig asks for on save. Turning it off suspends all of them at once -- the point being to stop formatting for a while without disabling the extension or hunting through per-language settings. Linting is unaffected: not wanting a file rewritten is not the same as not wanting to know what is wrong with it. There is a status bar switch for this next to the Poly item, and `Poly: Toggle Formatting` in the command palette.
config.deadCodeCodeLens.enabled.descript: Show an `analyze dead code` link on the first line of code in every file poly can answer about: Go (golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode), TypeScript and JavaScript (knip), Python (vulture). Clicking it runs `poly deadcode` in a terminal over that file's whole project — the go.work build list, the npm project, the Python project. Nothing runs until it is clicked: whole-program reachability costs a build, so it is asked rather than watched.
config.languageServers.description: Run the language server a project's own toolchain provides and route hover, go-to-definition, declaration, type definition, implementation, references, outline, completion, signature help, symbol highlight, folding, expand selection, rename and code actions to it. Nine are known: gopls (Go), rust-analyzer (Rust), clangd (C/C++), sourcekit-lsp (Swift), terraform-ls (Terraform), lua-language-server (Lua), bash-language-server (Shell), buf (Protobuf), arity (R). Code actions arrive as lightbulb actions only — the `source.*` kinds `editor.codeActionsOnSave` runs are left out, because VSCode runs those before the formatter and they would rewrite the same lines poly is about to format. Poly's own lint findings stay: the server's diagnostics are merged with them rather than replacing them, so selene and swiftlint keep reporting. Off by default: it overlaps with the official extension for that language, so remove that extension before turning this on. Poly never installs these servers — they come from PATH, and which features work is whatever the server itself declares.
config.languageServerLogs.description: Forward a downstream language server's own stderr to the Poly output channel. On by default. clangd and terraform-ls write a line per request; gopls, rust-analyzer, sourcekit-lsp and lua-language-server are quiet unless something is wrong. Turning this off discards that output entirely rather than asking each server to be quieter — not all of them can be. Poly's own reports, including a server that is missing or failed to start, are unaffected.
config.memoryLog.description: Write a line to the Poly output channel every time a file is opened or closed, saying what the daemon is holding: resident memory, how many documents and how many bytes of text, the lint and package caches, the findings each source is keeping, and which language servers are running. Off by default — it is a line per file in a log you also read to find out why a lint did not run. Turn it on when poly's memory looks wrong: the point of the line is that a rising number can be blamed on one of the caches rather than left as "the daemon got bigger". Read once at startup, so it takes a window reload.
config.updateCheck.enabled.description: Periodically check GitHub Releases for new Poly versions (also covers poly-syntax-highlight).
config.updateCheck.intervalDays.descript: Days between automatic update checks; 0 checks on every startup.
